ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\angle AOB = 90^{\circ}$, $\angle EOF = 60^{\circ}$, $OE$ bisects $\angle AOB$, and $OF$ bisects $\angle BOC$. What are the measures of $\angle AOC$ and $\angle COB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since OE bisects $\angle AOB$ and $\angle AOB=90^\circ$,
\[
\therefore \angle BOE = \angle AOB = 45^\circ,
\]
Also, since $\angle EOF=60^\circ$,
\[
\therefore \angle BOF = \angle EOF - \angle BOE= 15^\circ,
\]
And since OF bisects $\angle BOC$,
\[
\therefore \angle BOC=2\angle BOF=30^\circ,
\]
Thus, $\angle AOC=\angle AOB + \angle BOC=120^\circ$,
Hence, $\angle AOC=\boxed{120^\circ}$, $\angle COB=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $OE$ bisects $\angle AOB$ and $\angle AOB=90^\circ$, \[ \therefore \angle BOE = \angle AOB = 45^\circ, \] Also, since $\angle EOF=60^\circ$, \[ \therefore \angle BOF = \angle EOF - \angle BOE=15^\circ, \] And since $OF$ bisects $\angle BOC$, \[ \therefore \angle BOC=2\angle BOF=30^\circ, \] Thus, $\angle AOC=\angle AOB + \angle BOC=120^\circ$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, five rays are emitted from point O: OA is horizontal to the right, OB is vertical upward; OE is located between OA and OB; OF is located on the left side of OB; OC is farther left than OF. Therefore, OE and OF are respectively on the two sides of OB, and ∠EOF is composed of ∠EOB and ∠BOF added together. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOB = 90°, and OE bisects ∠AOB, so ∠EOB = 90° ÷ 2 = 45°. It is also known that ∠EOF = 60°; according to the order in the figure, ∠EOF = ∠EOB + ∠BOF, therefore ∠BOF = 60° − 45° = 15°. OF bisects ∠BOC, so ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BOF = 2 × 15° = 30°. Finally, ∠AOC crosses over ∠AOB and ∠BOC, so ∠AOC = 90° + 30° = 120°. Since ∠COB and ∠BOC are the same angle, ∠COB = 30°.
